prompt: Object P moves directly from A to C in 50 s. Object Q follows a longer route from A through B to C in 40 s. Compare, for the complete journeys, (a) their displacements, (b) their distances, (c) their average speeds and (d) their average velocities.

mark_scheme.criterion: States that the displacements are the same because both objects have the same start and finish positions.
States that Q travels a greater distance because Q follows the longer route.
States that the average speeds cannot be equal on the given information, with Q covering a greater distance in less time.
States that Q has the greater average velocity magnitude because the displacement is the same but Q takes less time; directions are the same.

hints: First separate quantities controlled by the route from quantities controlled only by start and finish.
Then compare each numerator and the journey times in the average-speed and average-velocity formulas.
solution: (a) Same displacement. (b) Q has greater distance. (c) Q has greater average speed. (d) Both average velocities have the same direction, but Q has greater magnitude because Q completes the same displacement in less time.
teacher_walkthrough: Both journeys begin at A and end at C. Displacement depends only on those positions, so both displacement vectors are the same.
Distance follows the route. Q uses the longer A-B-C route, so Q travels farther.
Average speed is total distance divided by total time. Q travels farther and takes less time, so Q's average speed is greater.
Average velocity is displacement divided by time. The displacement is the same, but Q takes 40 s instead of 50 s. Q therefore has the greater average velocity magnitude. Both point from A to C.
